title: Tetra-Fuse: Late Fusion Preserves Task-Specific Strengths of Heterogeneous Molecular Encoders for ADMET Prediction — code and model weights
description:
Code and model weights for the paper "Tetra-Fuse: Late Fusion Preserves Task-Specific Strengths of Heterogeneous Molecular Encoders for ADMET Prediction".

The release serves two independent uses. (1) Reproducing the paper: six self-contained Jupyter notebooks regenerate every main-text and supplementary figure and table from the released per-seed model predictions and leaderboard entries, with no GPU, no network, and no model weights required. (2) Predicting new molecules: the fine-tuned PEFT weights of all five Tetra-Fuse ensemble members (LoRA, AdapterGNN, fusion and head parameters, plus regression target scalers) are released here, together with an inference module and CLI that runs the k=5 uniform-mean ensemble on arbitrary SMILES across 22 TDC ADMET endpoints.

Also included: the qadmet training and evaluation engine, the 38 recipe YAMLs that reproduce the 10 base models, and the Polaris ADME-Fang external-benchmark integration.

The three pretrained backbones (CheMeleon, GraphMVP, MoLFormer) are not redistributed here — they are downloaded from their original authors; see weights/README.md. Only the parameters we trained are released, which is why the archive is 11.3 GiB rather than the ~78 GiB of raw training checkpoints.

Weight archives are per-member uncompressed tar files (the payload is dense fp32 tensors, where compression buys ~8%); every archive and metadata file ships with a SHA-256 checksum in zenodo_manifest.csv and SHA256SUMS.

Inference fidelity is verified rather than asserted: four of the five members reproduce the released predictions to floating-point tolerance, and the k=5 ensemble matches at three decimal places on every endpoint checked. See verification/inference_parity.md.
